status_summary: Executive Order 14276, signed 2025-04-17, directed the Commerce Secretary to review all marine national monuments within 180 days for possible opening to commercial fishing and to ask regional fishery management councils for updated recommendations; it does not mention national marine sanctuaries. Proclamation 10918 of the same day barred the Secretary from prohibiting commercial fishing in outer waters of the Pacific Remote Islands monument. Proclamation 11009 (signed 2026-02-06) restored commercial fishing in the Northeast Canyons and Seamounts monument, and Proclamation 11035 (signed 2026-06-11) removed monument fishing prohibitions in parts of the Papahanaumokuakea, Mariana Trench and Rose Atoll monuments and directed the Secretary to amend inconsistent regulations, including the Papahanaumokuakea National Marine Sanctuary regulations. Neither statute has been amended.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14276 directed a 180-day Commerce review of marine national monuments for commercial fishing and requests for updated regional council recommendations (published 2025-04-22).

Proclamation 10918 barred the Commerce Secretary from prohibiting commercial fishing by U.S.-flagged vessels in waters about 50 to 200 nautical miles from the Pacific Remote Islands monument's landward boundaries (published 2025-04-22).
Proclamation 11009 revoked the 2021 proclamation that had reinstated the commercial fishing ban in the Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument (published 2026-02-11).

Proclamation 11035 removed monument commercial fishing prohibitions in parts of the Papahanaumokuakea, Mariana Trench Islands Unit and Rose Atoll monuments for U.S.-flagged vessels and directed the Secretary to amend inconsistent regulations, including the Papahanaumokuakea sanctuary regulations (published 2026-06-17).
